speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash and tell me exactly where on your body it first appeared?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash consist of small, red, raised bumps that look like insect bites, and is it more severe on the trunk than on the face or limbs? I also need to know if she has any history of atopic dermatitis or recent exposure to other children with similar symptoms.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of a prodromal fever and rhinorrhea followed by a facial rash with perioral sparing and a trunk-predominant pruritic rash is classic for Erythema Infectiosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Fifth disease (Parvovirus B19 infection)
